svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Cloud WAN Flow Logs capture end-to-end attachment-to-attachment flows over a core network, with a record written at each attachment where traffic enters as ingress or leaves as egress. They publish to CloudWatch Logs, Amazon S3 or Amazon Data Firehose, and can be enabled on an entire core network, a single core network edge, or individual attachments. Collection happens outside the path of network traffic so throughput and latency are unaffected. Packet-header fields are exact: source and destination addresses, ports, protocol, packets and bytes. The Cloud WAN metadata that is the feature's reason to exist is not: segment names, Regions, attachment IDs and network function group attachment IDs are described in the documentation as best effort approximations whose values might be missing or inaccurate, because they do not come directly from the packet header. Segment IDs may also be briefly stale during initial propagation, and a flow might not be correlated end to end because of an internal system error or log propagation delay. Each record carries a log-status field with four values that state its own reliability: OK for normal logging, NODATA when there was no traffic during the aggregation interval, SKIPDATA when some records were skipped because of an internal capacity constraint or error, and INCOMPLETEDATA when the flow could not be fully captured so the record may be only partially complete, which means any analysis summing bytes without filtering on log-status is adding partial records to complete ones. Loss is attributed across four counters rather than reported as one figure: packets lost due to no route, due to a black hole, due to the size exceeding the MTU, and due to time-to-live expiration, each implying a different fix, with no route and blackhole being policy problems, MTU exceeded being a path-MTU problem and TTL expired suggesting a loop. Two scopes appear in the documentation but not the announcement: subscriptions can only be created in AWS Cloud WAN home Regions, and Cloud WAN currently supports only US West Oregon as the home Region, which cannot be changed once established, so this is a global-coverage feature with a single-Region control plane. Other limits are 250 subscriptions per resource per account, Tunnel-less Connect attachments unsupported with their flows appearing on the underlying transport VPC attachment, Route Table attachments unsupported with their flows appearing on the underlying peering connection, no real-time log streams, timestamps up to 60 seconds late, and a default record format that omits the two 1:1 NAT fields so a custom format is required to capture them. On cost, Cloud WAN introduces no additional charges but vended-logs ingestion and storage charges apply at each destination, and because a record is written at both ingress and egress one flow produces two records, which makes the three enablement scopes a cost control as much as a coverage one.
svg.title: Exact in the packet header, best effort in the Cloud WAN metadata
svg.text: The header fields are exact. The metadata that makes it Cloud WAN is not.
“Metadata fields that do not come directly from the packet header are best effort approximations, and their
values might be missing or inaccurate.”
FROM THE PACKET HEADER — EXACT
srcaddr dstaddr srcport dstport
protocol packets bytes
“which addresses talked, and how much”
CLOUD WAN METADATA — BEST EFFORT
src/dst-segment-name src/dst-region
cwan-attachment-id network-function-...
The reason to use this — and not evidence.
Each record states its own reliability — filter on log-status in every query
OK logging normally
NODATA “no network traffic … during the aggregation interval”
SKIPDATA records skipped — “internal capacity constraint, or an internal error”
INCOMPLETEDATA “might be only partially complete” — do not sum bytes blindly
Loss is attributed to a cause — the genuinely new telemetry
no-route / blackhole a policy problem: the segment cannot reach where it is going
mtu-exceeded path MTU — the classic hard-to-find global-network fault
ttl-expired suggests a loop. One aggregate figure would say something is wrong; these say who to call.
Global coverage, single-Region control plane — not in the announcement
“Subscriptions can only be created in AWS Cloud WAN home Regions.” And:
“Currently, Cloud WAN only supports US West (Oregon) as the home Region” — and you can’t change it.
Free at the source, two records per flow at the destination
“A flow log record is written at each attachment where traffic enters (ingress) or leaves (egress).” Cloud WAN
adds no charge; vended-logs ingestion does. The three enablement scopes are your cost control.
Also: 250 subscriptions per resource, no Tunnel-less Connect or Route Table attachments (flows appear on the
underlying transport or peering), no real-time streams, timestamps up to 60s late, 1:1 NAT fields off by default.
Packet-header fields are facts. Cloud WAN metadata is a strong hint. Keep the distinction downstream.
